children: on Wednesday ushered in a new era at its latest hardware event, headlined by new CEO John Ternus unveiling the company's first-ever foldable device alongside the AI-driven iPhone 18 Pro and heavily upgraded wearables.
Below is a breakdown of some of the biggest announcements from the high-profile event:
1. The foldable era begins with the iPhone Duo
highly anticipated entry into the foldable market was

by Ternus. Sized roughly like a passport, the $1,999 iPhone Duo features an aerospace titanium frame, dual batteries, and a 7.6-inch inner display that is 80% larger than the iPhone 18 Pro. Positioned as a productivity powerhouse, it supports the Apple Pencil and allows for split-screen multitasking.
2. iPhone 18 Pro elevates AI and camera capabilities

Powered by the new 2-nanometer A20 Pro chip and its dual neural engines, the iPhone 18 Pro models bring a 40% performance leap and deeper artificial intelligence integration. The standout hardware upgrade is a 48 MP Fusion main camera featuring a variable aperture for precise depth-of-field control, paired with a new Pro Controls system for manual adjustments.
3. Wearables gain audio intelligence and deeper health tracking
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4

a new S11-powered Health Sensing System that tracks vitals like heart rate and HRV significantly more frequently for better daily fitness insights. They also debut privacy-focused "audio intelligence" features—including Live Rewind, which transcribes the last 15 seconds of spoken audio, and Siri Recap for generating ambient conversational notes. Rounding out the updates, the new $129 AirPods 5 offer a refined open-ear fit with 50% more noise reduction than their predecessors.

title: 3 takeaways from Apple's iPhone launch event
